title: Architecture & Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Sara Kim
content:
Purpose:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and engineering standards across API design, coding practices, infrastructure, model-serving, observability, and performance. It also indexes active Decision Records (ADRs) relevant to these domains and prescribes default SLOs, thresholds, and rollout patterns for production services.

Scope:
Applies to all services and teams building customer-facing inference APIs, serving runtime components, and platform infrastructure (hosted, dedicated, and private deployments). Implementation and repo-level linters should enforce these standards.

Principles (summary):
- Developer ergonomics: APIs and infra should be predictable and easy for product engineers to adopt.
- Production-first: prioritize reliability, SLOs, and clear fallback behavior for inference endpoints.
- Observable and debuggable: every service exposes traces, structured logs, and key metrics by default.
- Cost-aware: architecture decisions must consider per-token cost, batching, and efficient resource usage.
- Backwards compatibility: breaking changes require an ADR and coordinated rollout.

1) API Standards:
Short intro: Public and internal REST/HTTP APIs must be consistent, discoverable, and versioned. Use OpenAPI v3 and publish spec artifacts to the internal API registry.
- Versioning: path-based major versioning (/v1/, /v2/). Minor non-breaking changes are documented in the OpenAPI spec and released under the same major version.
- Endpoint design: resource-oriented endpoints; avoid RPC verbs in resource names. Use POST for complex operations and query parameters for filtering.
- Request/response size limits: default payload body <= 1MB; streaming supported for long-running responses and token streams.
- Authentication: bearer tokens via Authorization header (JWT or API key). Sensitive endpoints require mTLS for private deployments.
- Error model: structured JSON with fields code, message, and details. Map HTTP codes: 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 500.
- Rate limiting and quotas: hosted API default policy: 100 requests/minute per API key; token-based soft quotas implemented separately. Dedicated customers have contract-configured limits.
- OpenAPI pipeline: OpenAPI generation and linting must run in CI; failing spec lint blocks merges.

2) Coding Standards:
- Languages: Go for control plane services, Rust/C++ for runtime hot paths, Python for SDKs and eval tooling.
- Linters and formatters: enable gofmt/golangci-lint, rustfmt/clippy, black/ruff for Python. CI runs format + lint.
- Dependency management: explicit versions (go.mod, Cargo.lock, pinned pip requirements). Weekly vulnerability scans.
- Testing targets: unit test coverage target >= 80% for core modules; integration tests for cross-service contracts; nightly E2E runs for model-serving flows.
- Code reviews: minimum one approver from owning team and one reviewer from infra or security for public-facing changes. Large cross-service changes require a design review doc linked in the PR.
- Secret handling: never commit credentials. Use Vault or KMS-backed secret store; CI must avoid echoing secrets.

3) Infrastructure Standards:
- IaC: Terraform is canonical for cloud resources. Modules live in infra/terraform-modules and follow the inputs/outputs/owners pattern.
- Environment parity: minimize behavior differences between dev/staging/prod. Use feature flags, not separate code paths, for behavioural changes.
- Networking: service-to-service auth via mTLS; default deny egress and explicit allowlists; VPC peering for Private deployments.
- Instance sizing: GPU fleets use pinned instance classes (e.g., A100-40GB, H100 family). Autoscaling with predictive policies for burst capacity.
- Disaster recovery: daily snapshots for stateful stores. Control plane RTO target = 30 minutes; RPO = 15 minutes.

4) Model-serving Standards:
- Model packaging: every model artifact must include a metadata.txt or metadata.json with model_id, version, tokenizer, quantization profile, expected_max_seq, and owner.
- Quantization and variants: store quantized variants alongside FP16/FP32 artifacts. Model catalog must advertise available variants.
- KV-cache and prefix caching: transformer-serving endpoints must support KV cache reuse and accept prefix-cache hints from clients.
- Rollout policy for model updates: canary at 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated performance and quality gates at each step.
- Model SLOs: per-token tail latency (p99) targets: small models <= 60ms, medium <= 120ms, large <= 250ms (hosted defaults). Throughput SLOs tracked per instance class.
- Fallbacks: automatic fallback to compatible lighter variants under capacity pressure or degraded latency, subject to QA gating.

5) Observability Standards:
- Metrics: Prometheus-compatible metrics are required. Instrumentations required: request_duration_seconds, request_latency_ms_bucket, requests_total{status,route}, model_tokens_generated_total, cache_hits_total, cache_misses_total.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry is standard. Propagate traceparent across RPCs. Sampling: 100% for errors, 5% for successes (adjustable by service).
- Logging: structured JSON logs containing timestamp, level, service, trace_id, request_id, message, and attributes. PII must be filtered before logging.
- Dashboards and alerts: standard dashboards for latency, error rate, p95/p99, and token cost per route. Primary alerts: error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, p99 latency > 2x target for 10 minutes, streaming failure rate > 0.5% for 10 minutes.
- Cost observability: per-route token counts and GPU-hours exposed through billing metrics and dashboards.

6) Performance Standards:
- Benchmarks: release gating requires perf regression tests against a committed baseline harness. Baselines recorded monthly for each major model family and runtime kernel set.
- SLOs: control plane availability 99.95% (hosted control plane endpoints), model serving availability 99.9% (tier-dependent).
- Load testing: services must provide steady-state and spike tests. Significant changes must run canary perf runs and collect GPU flame graphs.
- Optimization targets: first-token latency under 100ms for chat workloads on recommended hardware for medium models; per-token cost budgets documented per route.

7) Decision Records (ADRs) - active and recent:
Include and reference ADRs when proposing related changes. Key ADRs:
- ADR-2025-01: Model Variant Fallback Policy (approved 2025-01-20). Prefers automatic fallback to compatible quantized variants during capacity constraints, with QA gating.
- ADR-2025-07: OpenAPI-first API Design (approved 2025-07-15). APIs are defined in OpenAPI with SDKs generated automatically.
- ADR-2026-02: Default Observability Stack (approved 2026-02-10). Standardize telemetry on OpenTelemetry + Prometheus + Grafana + Tempo.
- ADR-2026-05: Quantization Profiles (approved 2026-05-18). Standardize int8 and fp16 profiles and require quantization perf tests.

ADR example (short): ADR-2026-02 Default Observability Stack
- Status: accepted
- Context: multiple overlapping tracing solutions caused gaps in trace coverage and high maintenance.
- Decision: standardize on OTel collectors, Prometheus exporters, Grafana dashboards, and Tempo for trace storage.
- Consequences: migration effort; improved trace continuity and standard sampling rates.

8) Release & Rollout Playbook (summary):
- Pre-merge: unit + lint + OpenAPI spec checks must pass.
- Canary: deploy canary to 1% traffic for 30 minutes; run smoke, perf, and quality probes; expand to 10% and run automated regression evals; continue expansion after gates pass.
- Rollback: automated rollback triggers on critical alerts or quality regression beyond thresholds. Rollback steps documented in service runbooks.

9) Ownership and Governance:
- Standards owner: Eng Architecture (primary) with eng-platform and applied-ml-and-evals as operational and quality co-owners.
- Review cadence: quarterly review of standards and ADRs. ADR proposals submitted using the ADR template and emailed to eng-architecture@redwood.com.

10) Appendix: Required CI checks (example list):
- openapi-lint (required)
- unit-tests (coverage thresholds)
- integration-tests (model-serving smoke)
- perf-regression-check (no regressions > 3% median or > 5% p95)
- security-scan (critical/high vulnerabilities block)
